demons seizing the nations as pagan gods

To show the prophecy speaks of Christ: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, and the apostle explains, how will they call on one they have not believed, and how will they preach unless they are sent? Jesus called the twelve and gave them power over demons, and the Spirit said, set apart Paul and Barnabas for the work.
the sending of preachers by Christ and the Holy Spirit

The stone cut out without hands is Christ born without a man, without the union of marriage, and it grew into a great mountain filling the earth; human births are called stone-cuttings, as Isaiah says, look to the rock you were hewn from, to Abraham your father and Sarah who bore you.
the stone cut without hands as the virgin birth

Rejoice, daughter of Zion, your king comes meek and humble, riding a colt; meekness and humility come first to show it was not poverty, since the King of powers who has countless chariots and rides on the wings of the wind chose a donkey out of humility.
the king's humility in riding a donkey into Jerusalem

The lyre is not evil in itself but became an instrument of passion; when it sang praises to God it was not unclean, as David says praise the Lord with harp and lyre and cymbals, and David's playing drove away the evil spirit that troubled Saul; every art was made to please God.
musical instruments in worship and David's harp calming Saul

The heretics slander us everywhere as if the Church preached three almighties, but we only repeat the prophets: the Church knows not three almighty beings but one power that holds all things, known in Father, Son and Holy Spirit; anathema to anyone who says three separate gods.
one almighty God, not three: the Trinity against tritheism

A teacher who speaks does not empty his own mind; the word goes out to many ears yet stays with its source, so how could the divine Word that appeared in the world leave the Father's bosom empty, or his begetting involve division? Search the Scriptures: God gave the text but hid its meaning to exercise your mind.
the generation of the Word compared with human speech

Why did he say, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me? Not out of compulsion or cowardice, but as part of the human economy, sparing those who would stumble, since he knew the cross would scandalize many, a stumbling block to Jews and folly to Gentiles.
the prayer in Gethsemane: let this cup pass from me

He did not say whoever calls on my name will be saved, but on the name of the Lord; Paul, the interpreter of the prophets, asks whether God is God of the Jews only and not the Gentiles too, since one God justifies the circumcised and the uncircumcised by faith.
salvation for Jews and Gentiles by calling on the Lord's name

Heretics are a garden of cucumbers: whatever they plant has no hope, because whoever follows his own mind instead of God's word plants unbelief; the heavenly Father plants through prophets and apostles, Satan through heretics, and every plant my Father has not planted will be uprooted.
heresy as plants not planted by the Father

Purify your soul and scrape off the rust; don't be a believer in church and a heretic outside; a light soul changes with circumstances, but the God-fearing stays the same in war, famine and plenty, unmoved by trouble and not made lazy by comfort.
steadfastness of the God-fearing soul in changing circumstances

There was no necessity or fixed limit imposed on the Saviour from above; it was his own economy and will, as he said: no one takes my life from me, I have power to lay it down and take it up again; so when he says let this cup pass, he says it for your weakness, not his own.
Christ's voluntary death and the cup in Gethsemane

The word of preaching is a net: the fisherman casts it without knowing what it has caught in the hidden depths, and so the preacher does not know whom the divine word has caught, but God, who examines the net, knows which fish was taken, which of the Spirit-fighters or Arians was drawn to Christ.
preaching as a fishing net

As the cross approached, the Lord knew that heretics would rise against the truth and deny his real sufferings, especially the followers of Mani who claimed his passion was a shadow and an illusion and that he had no real body, so he silenced them in advance by showing he had put on a body that suffers.
against the Manichaeans: Christ's real body and real suffering

The whole earth was filled with the knowledge of the Lord as waters cover the sea: rivers from every land pour into the sea without covering it, but the gospel did what nature cannot, spreading to every corner of the earth and covering the sea in which people were tossing as in an abyss.
the gospel filling the earth as waters cover the sea

Earthly people go to meet kings with their own chariots and horses, but the Saviour sends heavenly envoys, chariots of cloud; Elijah was taken up in a chariot of fire, but the apostles and others on clouds, and the fiery one is not more honourable than the cloud.
Elijah's chariot of fire and the clouds of the ascension

Let us now wait for our spiritual father, the true teacher of the Church, and say to him: awake, my glory, awake, harp and lyre, for we need your teaching; however much flour there is, a little leaven is needed, so we need your fatherly help to confirm our words.
a preacher yielding the pulpit to the bishop

After the deacon's call of peace, the priest takes the cross from the archdeacon and gives it to a deacon, and the Gospel book to another; they stand before the altar facing each other, cross on the south and Gospel on the north, kiss them and lay them on the holy table, while the priest says: let your priests be clothed with righteousness.
procession of the cross and Gospel to the altar

The priest stands at the altar door and blesses the people aloud: he who blessed us with every spiritual blessing through Jesus Christ, who told his disciples that whoever eats my body and drinks my blood abides in me and I will raise him on the last day, may he bless our congregation and seal you with the sign of the cross.
the final blessing and dismissal of the Eucharist

The priest censes his hands, saying: our Lord and God, sweeten the stench of our uncleanness with the fragrance of your love, good shepherd who went out to seek us, forgive my sins known and unknown; then he blesses the deacon, the people and the altar set up in the likeness of our Lord's tomb.
censing the hands before the fraction; the altar as Christ's tomb

Glory to him who forgave our debts by his body and wiped out our sins by his blood; for the departed: hear, Lord, the voice of our prayer, accept our sacrifices and forgive the debts of our dead, like the first offering that Abel brought.
prayer for the departed at the Eucharist

By the prayers of our holy father, the confessors and Mar George, and the power of the cross, let us ask Christ for mercy on our souls; Lord, I call to you, answer me; let my prayer rise like incense before you and the lifting of my hands like the evening offering; set a guard over my mouth.
evening prayer: let my prayer rise like incense

If there are no subdeacons or readers, unordained boys may serve the mysteries in alb and girdle; the archdeacon may prepare the bread and wine in place of the priest; only ordained deacons may carry the paten and hold the chalice; feasts of our Lord are called dominical and those of the saints commemorations.
rubrics on who may serve at the altar

The living, life-giving bread that came down from heaven gives life to the whole world; those who eat it do not die; whoever approaches in love and receives me lives in me forever and inherits the kingdom; here the priest kisses the host crosswise without touching it with his lips.
the bread of life that came down from heaven

Rescue me from my persecutors, for they are stronger than I; bring me out of prison so I may praise your name; your word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my path; I have sworn to keep your righteous judgments. Praise the Lord, all you nations.
your word is a lamp to my feet

Response: Lord, forgive the sins and follies of your servants. Deacon: with souls cleansed of hatred and enmity, let us receive the holy thing in harmony and be sanctified by the Holy Spirit, that the mysteries may be for the resurrection of our bodies and the salvation of our souls.
the litany before communion

Lord God, protect with the right hand of your mercy the holy apostolic catholic Church from one end of the earth to the other, keep it from all harm hidden and open, and make us all worthy to serve you purely and to please you all our days with good works.
prayer for the protection of the whole Church

O Lord God almighty, accept this offering for the head of the catholic Church, our patriarch, and for our bishop, for the whole holy Church, for priests, kings and rulers, in honour of the prophets, apostles, martyrs and confessors, and for the mourning, the poor, the oppressed, the sick and the departed.
intercessions for the patriarch, the Church and the departed

The choir is split into two; new hymns may not be introduced without church permission; the priest says the quiet prayer with head bowed and hands crossed; the Gospel and readings are read from the bema in the middle of the nave, with seats for the priest and archdeacon on one side and the deacons on the other.
rubrics for the readings, choir and bema

Turning to the people with arms open he says: my brothers, pray for me that this offering may be completed by my hands; they answer: may Christ hear your prayers and accept your offering; with the heavenly powers we confess you, Lord, and your hidden Son who, being in your image, did not count equality a thing to be grasped but emptied himself.
the priest asking the people to pray for him before the anaphora

Lord Christ, unworthy as I am, I carry the riches of your mercies and your fearful mystery; the priest receives the mysteries with fear and love and lifts the chalice: the cup of your precious blood, mixed at your banquet for your guests, O heavenly bridegroom, and drinks it carefully.
the priest's communion: the cup of the heavenly bridegroom

We ask for forgiveness of sins and whatever helps our lives and pleases your divinity; we commit our souls and one another to the Father, Son and Holy Spirit; then they open the altar veil, and the priest stands on the bema with arms outstretched praying that God pour his gifts through our hands.
the end of the litany and the opening of the altar veil

To the great, fearful, holy and incomprehensible name of your glorious Trinity we owe thanks and worship at all times; the deacon brings the censer and the priest blesses the incense quietly in the name of the Trinity, then puts three grains of frankincense on the coals.
blessing of incense in the name of the Trinity

Thousands of thousands on high and myriads of holy angels bless and worship your majesty; with the holy cherubim and seraphim they cry out without ceasing: holy, holy, holy Lord God almighty, heaven and earth are full of his praises, hosanna in the highest, blessed is he who came and is coming.
the Sanctus: angels crying holy, holy, holy

They recite the faith of the three hundred and eighteen bishops gathered at Nicaea in Bithynia in the days of the victorious emperor Constantine, who met because of the wickedness of Arius, as has been the custom in the holy apostolic Church of the East from the earliest days.
the Nicene creed of the 318 fathers against Arius

Blessed are those whose way is blameless, alleluia, who walk in the law of the Lord; blessed are those who keep his testimonies and seek him with all their heart; you commanded your precepts to be kept carefully; how can a young man keep his way pure?
blessed are the blameless who walk in the law of the Lord

My brothers, receive the body of the Son, says the Church, and drink his cup in faith in the house of the kingdom; the priest gives the holy body saying: the body of our Lord Jesus Christ to the discerning believer for the forgiveness of debts, and the deacon gives the cup of his precious blood.
giving communion to the faithful
